findings.claim: The ACDSL policy self-management gate is fully bypassable in one commit: because base_ref inside the attacker-editable acdsl/policy.json is used verbatim as the only candidate ref, an agent can set base_ref to HEAD (or its own branch), making basePolicy read the attacker's own malicious policy as ground truth and defeating gated/strict enforcement entirely.
findings.fix: Don't let the file under test choose its own authoritative ref: resolve the base only from hardcoded upstream candidates (origin/HEAD, origin/main, main, master), or if an override is needed, source base_ref from outside policySurface's attacker-reachable scope and verify the candidate ref is reachable from an origin/* tracking ref (e.g. git merge-base --is-ancestor) before trusting anything read from it; add a fail-base-ref-self-reference test alongside TestCheckPolicyUnresolvableBase.

findings.claim: handleRepoWorktreeStatus reads the status-cache entry once up front and never reassigns it when a fresh scan fails, so a stale ScannedAt (or zero time on a first-ever failed scan) is rendered next to the fresh-scan error banner.
findings.fix: Only set data.ScannedAt from entry.ScannedAt when data.Cached is true or the fresh scan succeeded; otherwise leave it zero and have the template treat zero as "no successful scan yet".

findings.claim: The unattended nightly orchestrate stage rewrites the operator's live ~/.claude/settings.json via jq + mv with no pre-write validation of the tmp file and no backup, so a logically bad write (e.g. from a malformed repos.json jq tolerates) silently degrades every future session's permissions.
findings.fix: Validate the tmp file parses and that .permissions.additionalDirectories is still an array of strings before the mv, and keep one rotated backup (settings.json.bak), following the repo's existing pattern (check sync_settings.sh) rather than inventing a new one.

findings.claim: Because the smine repo's own committed acdsl/policy.json sets mode "free", the gated/strict CheckPolicy code paths are never exercised by make audit's acdsl check step, leaving the feature's only automated coverage in unit tests and the plan's gated/strict verification scenario a manual step, so a regression like finding #1 would ship silently.
findings.fix: Either add a dedicated CI step that runs acdsl dist into a scratch repo and asserts a known-bad gated/strict scenario is caught (automating the plan's manual verification scenarios), or record this as a tracked gap per ACTION-REVIEW-DOCS-004 rather than leaving it implicit.

findings.claim: The Bash branch of the context-read denial only recognizes a bare two-token cat command, so head/less/command-substitution variants sail through unexamined — trivially bypassable if ever treated as a real boundary rather than an advisory nudge.
findings.fix: None required; consider tightening the top-of-file comment to state explicitly that this is a UX nudge only, not a boundary, matching the wording of acdsl-policy-guard.sh's doc comment.

findings.claim: bootstrapEnv's extra-prompt validation blocks quotes and newlines but not all shell-meaningful characters, which is safe today (env var / argv only, never eval'd) but would become insufficient if a future refactor interpolated the prompt into a script.
findings.fix: No fix needed now; just don't let a future refactor move this into an eval-based path without re-deriving the validation.
